sections.en: Benefit: Know that the brother of the grandfather and the maternal uncle of the grandfather and the wife of the grandfather have no place in the four quadrants, they do not fall in any of these, neither five, nor seven, nor eight from the place of the ascendant which is after it. And of these houses of the ascendant, the second, fifth, eighth, and eleventh are called succedent (zawayid), and the ninth, third, twelfth, and sixth are called cadent (zayil al-awtad) and they are poles. And the sixth and twelfth from the ascendant. And stronger than all houses is the ascendant, and the margin, then the fourth, then the tenth, then the seventh, then the eleventh, then the fifth, then the ninth, then the third, then the eighth and second, then the ninth and twelfth. And know that all houses are cadent, and these twelve are called the ditch and hope, and one of the extremes of the house is called the four quadrants. The first quadrant is from the ascendant, the ascendant, and it is masculine and a peg, up to the fourth, and it is feminine and a peg. The ascending quadrant is opposite the descending quadrant, and opposite the feminine quadrant is, and opposite the ascending is descending. And of the houses of the ascendant, whatever is named after it is divorced, like the third and fifth which were, and whatever is even is called feminine.

summary.headline: Judgments of the Twelve Houses
summary.text: Judgments of the twelve astrological houses, listing their associations with life, wealth, kinship, travel, fathers, children, illness, women, enemies, religion, rank, hopes, sovereignty, and quadrupeds. The marginal note classifies succedent and cadent houses, quadrants, masculine and feminine houses, and the relative strength of the houses; the text also maps houses to paternal and maternal uncles and the sultan’s household.
